You make a map that answers a question about this codebase, for someone semi-technical. Explore with Read, Grep and Glob, then return the map as JSON. You cannot edit anything.

## The question
"How does the Claude skill logic work to start a map? Walk through what happens from the moment a map is requested until Claude has drafted it."

## What a good map is
- It follows what happens, in order, from where it starts (a button, a route, a job, a command) to where it ends (a table write, an email, an outside API), or to where it stops.
- 2–6 `areas` named in product language (Patients, Billing, Background jobs), not folder names.
- 4–12 boxes (`nodes`). Each is one step a person would recognize. `name`: plain English, at most 30 characters ("Patient marked enrolled", not "markConverted()").
- `kind`: entry (a way in), step, store (table, queue, cache), external (outside service), job (scheduled or background work).
- `explain` for every box: `concept` (1–2 plain sentences, no jargon), `how` (the mechanism; define any term you use), `code` (function and file names).
- Arrow `label`: 1–3 words saying how one step leads to the next ("sends request", "calls", "announces", "every night").
- When the trail stops, or something that should be connected isn't, record an `absence`: the `claim` in plain words, the two boxes it should connect (`between`), and the exact `search` that proves nothing is there (`pattern`, `regex`, optional `paths` globs), with `matches` set to the count that search returns (usually 0). Run that search yourself with Grep first.
- Code that exists but isn't reached from the start can still be boxes. Don't draw arrows that don't exist; use an absence.

## Evidence rules (a program checks every claim; anything it can't confirm is shown as unconfirmed)
- Every box and arrow cites at least one line: `file` (repo-relative), `line` (1-based), and `text` copied exactly from that line. A distinctive fragment of 10–80 characters works best.
- A box that is a function or method gets `symbol`: "<file>#<name>", named the way the checker names it: methods as Class.method, object members as obj.member ("src/db.ts#db.update"), a function inside another function as outer.inner, and a function in the object a factory returns as factory.member. When a list of functions by file is given, copy the name from it. If you aren't sure of the name, leave `symbol` out: the box is still checked by its cited line.
- Arrow `kind`: `calls` when a function in the from box literally calls the function in the to box; `request` when an HTTP call in the from box hits a route handled by the to box; `imports`; `then` for anything else (events, ordering). The checker verifies calls, request and imports against the code, so use them only when literally true.
- Never cite or read secret files (.env, keys).

## Walkthrough (`tour`, written last)
- 4–7 stops in the order a newcomer should read them: what the map shows → the path → the problem, if there is one → what it means.
- Each stop: `title`, `text` (2–3 plain sentences), `focus` (ids of the areas, nodes, edges or absences it's about), optional `terms` it uses that need defining, and `ask` with 1–2 good next questions.
- Point stops only at boxes, arrows and absences you're confident in.

4	---
5	
6	# codemap
7	
8	codemap turns a question about this repo into a map the person can explore in their browser: areas of the app, the
9	steps in order, labeled arrows, and red dashed arrows where something that should be connected isn't. A plain program
10	checks every claim against the code before it's shown. In the map they can take a walkthrough, select any box or arrow
11	and ask about it, and approve fixes that codemap applies and re-checks.
12	
13	## When to use it
14	
15	- The user asks how something works across several files: "what happens when…", "how does X reach Y", "where does Z
16	  get triggered".
17	- The user is about to change code they don't understand yet and wants to see it first.
18	- The user asks for a map, diagram, graph or walkthrough of part of the code.
19	
20	Don't use it for a question about a single line or function; answer that directly.
21	
22	## How to run it
23	
24	Run from the repo root (or pass `--repo`). Use the user's question in their own words:
25	
26	```bash
27	codemap "What happens when a patient converts?" --repo "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
28	```
29	
30	It starts a small local server and opens the map in the user's browser by itself, where they watch Claude explore
31	(about a minute for a small repo). Don't pass `--no-open`. It also prints the link
32	(`http://127.0.0.1:4317/m/<id>?t=<token>`): tell the user the map is opening, and give them the link in case the tab
33	didn't appear. Run the command in the background and don't wait for it to exit. Don't stop it yourself either: it stops
34	on its own a little after the user closes the last codemap tab (never while Claude is still working), or when they
35	press Stop codemap on the page. If a codemap server is already running, the new one picks another free port.
36	
37	Other commands:
38	
39	- `codemap open` lists the maps already made in this repo (they're saved under `.codemap/maps/`).
40	- `codemap check <map-id>` re-checks a saved map against the current code and prints anything that no longer holds.
41	  It exits with 1 if a claim fails, so it can run in CI.
42	
43	## Notes
44	
45	- codemap reads the code and never changes it, except for a fix the user approves in the map.
46	- It never reads secret files (`.env`, keys) and only listens on 127.0.0.1.
47	- It needs Claude access: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or a logged-in Claude Code.
48	- If `codemap` isn't on the PATH, it hasn't been installed. Tell the user to install it from the codemap repo
49	  (see its README) instead of guessing another command.
50

1	// Making a map: a head start from the code facts, Claude explores and drafts, the checker re-reads the code, and Claude
2	// gets up to `repairs` chances to fix what didn't check out. A repair returns only the changes (`patchMap`), not the
3	// whole map again, since writing the map is most of the time a map takes. The best attempt wins; nothing unconfirmed
4	// is hidden.
5	import { check, parseMap, patchMap, type CheckReport, type CodeMap, type ParseResult } from '@codemap/core';
6	import type { Agent, Progress } from './agent';
7	import { headStart, symbolIndexOf } from './hints';
8	import { evidenceRepairPrompt, makerPrompt, patchRepairPrompt, shapeRepairPrompt } from './prompts';
9	import { MAP_PATCH_SCHEMA, MAP_SCHEMA, RawMapPatch } from './schemas';
10	
11	export type Status = { kind: 'status'; text: string };
12	export type MakeOptions = {
13	  root: string;
14	  question: string;
15	  agent: Agent;
16	  model?: string;
17	  repairs?: number;
18	  onProgress?: (p: Progress | Status) => void;
19	  signal?: AbortSignal;
20	};
21	export type MakeResult = { map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport; sessionId: string | null; cost: number; rounds: number };
22	
23	const withQuestion = (output: unknown, question: string) =>
24	  output && typeof output === 'object' ? { ...(output as Record<string, unknown>), version: 1, question } : output;
25	
26	/** Claude's changes applied to the map they're for, or what stops them from applying. */
27	function applyPatch(map: CodeMap, output: unknown): ParseResult {
28	  const raw = RawMapPatch.safeParse(output);
29	  if (!raw.success) return { ok: false, problems: raw.error.issues.map((i) => `${i.path.join('.') || '(changes)'}: ${i.message}`) };
30	  return patchMap(map, raw.data);
31	}
32	
33	export async function makeMap(o: MakeOptions): Promise<MakeResult> {
34	  const status = (text: string) => o.onProgress?.({ kind: 'status', text });
35	  status('Scanning the code for ways in, routes and tables');
36	  const hints = await headStart(o.root);
37	  const symbolsIn = symbolIndexOf(hints.scan);
38	  status('Claude is exploring the code');
39	  const run = (prompt: string, resume: string | null, schema: Record<string, unknown>) =>
40	    o.agent({ prompt, schema, cwd: o.root, resume, model: o.model, onProgress: o.onProgress, signal: o.signal });
41	
42	  let res = await run(makerPrompt(o.question, hints.text), null, MAP_SCHEMA);
43	  let cost = res.cost ?? 0;
44	  let rounds = 1;
45	  let best: { map: CodeMap; report: CheckReport } | null = null;
46	  let lastProblems: string[] = [];
47	  /** What the last reply is: a whole map, or changes to `current`, the last map that could be read. */
48	  let reply: 'map' | 'patch' = 'map';
49	  let current: CodeMap | null = null;
50	
51	  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
52	    const parsed: ParseResult = reply === 'map' || !current ? parseMap(withQuestion(res.output, o.question)) : applyPatch(current, res.output);
53	    let repair: { prompt: string; reply: 'map' | 'patch' } | null = null;
54	    if (!parsed.ok) {
55	      lastProblems = parsed.problems;
56	      repair = current ? { prompt: patchRepairPrompt(parsed.problems), reply: 'patch' } : { prompt: shapeRepairPrompt(parsed.problems), reply: 'map' };
57	    } else {
58	      current = parsed.map;
59	      status('Checking every claim against the code');
60	      const report = check(parsed.map, o.root);
61	      if (!best || report.summary.unconfirmed < best.report.summary.unconfirmed) best = { map: parsed.map, report };
62	      status(`${report.summary.confirmed} of ${report.summary.claims} claims confirmed`);
63	      if (report.summary.unconfirmed > 0) repair = { prompt: evidenceRepairPrompt(report, symbolsIn), reply: 'patch' };
64	    }
65	    if (!repair || attempt >= (o.repairs ?? 2)) break;
66	    status(parsed.ok ? 'Asking Claude to fix the claims that didn\'t check out' : current ? 'Asking Claude to fix its changes' : 'Asking Claude to fix the map\'s structure');
67	    res = await run(repair.prompt, res.sessionId, repair.reply === 'map' ? MAP_SCHEMA : MAP_PATCH_SCHEMA);
68	    reply = repair.reply;
69	    cost += res.cost ?? 0;
70	    rounds++;
71	  }
72	  if (!best) throw new Error(`Claude's map couldn't be read: ${lastProblems.slice(0, 5).join('; ')}`);
73	  return { ...best, sessionId: res.sessionId, cost, rounds };
74	}

28	const NOT_SECRETS = '!**/{.env,.env.*,*.pem,*.key,*.p12,id_rsa*,id_ed25519*,.npmrc,.netrc}';
29	
30	/** A plain-English progress line for a tool call, with paths relative to the repo. */
31	export function progressOf(name: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, cwd: string): Progress | null {
32	  const rel = (p: unknown) => (typeof p === 'string' ? path.relative(cwd, path.resolve(cwd, p)) || '.' : '');
33	  if (name === 'Read') return { kind: 'read', text: `Reading ${rel(input.file_path)}` };
34	  if (name === 'Grep') return { kind: 'search', text: `Searching for "${String(input.pattern ?? '')}"${input.path ? ` in ${rel(input.path)}` : ''}` };
35	  if (name === 'Glob') return { kind: 'list', text: `Looking for files matching ${String(input.pattern ?? '')}` };
36	  return null;
37	}
38	
39	/** Refuse secret files, and keep repo-wide searches away from them. */
40	export function secretGuard(cwd: string): HookCallback {
41	  return async (input) => {
42	    const i = input as PreToolUseHookInput;
43	    const ti = (i.tool_input ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
44	    const target = typeof ti.file_path === 'string' ? ti.file_path : typeof ti.path === 'string' ? ti.path : null;
45	    const rel = target ? path.relative(cwd, path.resolve(cwd, target)) : null;
46	    if (rel && (rel.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(rel))) {
47	      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: 'Only files inside this repo can be read.' } };
48	    }
49	    if (rel && isSecretPath(rel)) {
50	      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'deny', permissionDecisionReason: 'Secret files are never read.' } };
51	    }
52	    if (i.tool_name === 'Grep' && ti.glob === undefined && ti.type === undefined) {
53	      return { hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'PreToolUse', permissionDecision: 'allow', updatedInput: { ...ti, glob: NOT_SECRETS } } };
54	    }
55	    return {};
56	  };
57	}

59	export const sdkAgent: Agent = async (req) => {
60	  const abortController = new AbortController();

63	  const tools = READ_ONLY.filter((t) => (req.tools ?? READ_ONLY).includes(t));
64	  const q = query({
65	    prompt: req.prompt,
66	    options: {
67	      cwd: req.cwd,
68	      model: req.model ?? DEFAULT_MODEL,
69	      tools,
70	      allowedTools: tools,
71	      permissionMode: 'dontAsk',
72	      settingSources: [],
73	      strictMcpConfig: true,
74	      outputFormat: { type: 'json_schema', schema: req.schema },
75	      maxTurns: req.maxTurns ?? 60,
76	      abortController,
77	      hooks: { PreToolUse: [{ matcher: 'Read|Grep|Glob', hooks: [secretGuard(req.cwd)] }] },
78	      ...(req.resume ? { resume: req.resume } : {}),
79	    },
80	  });
81	  let sessionId: string | null = null;
82	  for await (const m of q) {
83	    if ('session_id' in m && typeof m.session_id === 'string') sessionId = m.session_id;
84	    if (m.type === 'assistant' && !m.parent_tool_use_id) {
85	      for (const block of m.message.content) {
86	        if (block.type !== 'tool_use') continue;
87	        const p = progressOf(block.name, (block.input ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>, req.cwd);
88	        if (p) req.onProgress?.(p);

90	    }
91	    if (m.type === 'result') {
92	      if (m.subtype !== 'success' || m.structured_output === undefined) {
93	        throw Object.assign(new Error(`Claude stopped before answering (${m.subtype}).`), { cost: m.total_cost_usd });
94	      }
95	      return { output: m.structured_output, sessionId, cost: m.total_cost_usd };
96	    }
97	  }
98	  throw new Error('Claude returned no result.');
99	};
